title: Boreas configuration
description: The on-disk configuration contract. Unknown fields are warnings, not errors (forward compatibility). Values outside a range are clamped by the loader where a safe clamp exists (sampling interval, watchdog timeout, panic threshold per ADR 0022) and refused where repair would hide a mistake (curves). A broken file never crashes the application: it falls back to the last valid configuration and the fans stay with the firmware (invariant G6).

schemaVersion.description: Increased only with a migration function proven lossless by a test. A pre-migration backup is written automatically.

panicTemperatureCelsius.description: K3 trigger. The ceiling is the default (95): the threshold may be lowered, never raised (G2, ADR 0022).

watchdogTimeoutSeconds.description: Locked range (G3); cannot be disabled. READ ONLY in this build: the helper reads no configuration (M5) and the XPC surface is exactly four methods (M4), so there is no way to deliver a different timeout to it. The helper derives its own timeout from the shared heartbeat constants. See ADR 0023.

curve.description: Control points, strictly increasing in celsius, non-decreasing in duty. Validated on load; an invalid curve is refused, never repaired silently.

group.description: A sensor group name, e.g. compute, compute.performance, graphics, storage.

perFan.description: Per-fan overrides, keyed by the fan id as a string ("0", "1", ...).

curve.description: Control points, strictly increasing in celsius, non-decreasing in duty. Validated on load; an invalid curve is refused, never repaired silently.

group.description: A sensor group name, e.g. compute, compute.performance, graphics, storage.

triggers.description: The profile activates when ANY trigger holds. Manual selection is not a trigger; it beats every trigger.

hysteresis.description: Band width in celsius. 0 disables the effect.

enginePaused.description: True on the System profile: the firmware keeps the fans.

defaultProfileName.description: The profile arbitration falls back to when no trigger holds and nothing is selected manually.

sensorOverrides.description: Per-sensor corrections keyed by the sensor's raw hardware name. Optional and additive: a file without this section is valid.

displayName.description: Replaces the normalised name shown in the interface.

group.description: Re-files the sensor into another group, which also changes which curves can bind to it.

hidden.description: Keeps the sensor out of the interface. It is still read, still counted by its group's aggregate and still able to trigger the panic layer - hiding is a display choice, never a safety one.

notifications.description: Notification triggers and noise control (P7.01). Optional and additive: a file without this section is valid and means the defaults, which leave notifications OFF. The permission macOS requires is requested when the user switches them on, never at launch.

isEnabled.description: The master switch. False by default: delivering a notification needs the user's permission, and this application does not ask for one until asked to.

suppressionWindowMinutes.description: A notification of the same kind and subject does not repeat inside this window. Clamped into range by the type; a value outside it is corrected, not refused.

enabledKinds.description: Which triggers fire once notifications are enabled. 'panicEngaged' is always delivered whether or not it appears here, and no noise-control mechanism can drop it — the same reasoning as G2 one level up.

quietHours.description: A window of the day in which ordinary notifications are held back. Spans midnight when start > end, which is the usual case. Full-speed cooling is still announced.

startMinuteOfDay.description: Minutes from midnight. Out-of-range values wrap rather than clamp, so 1500 means 01:00 the next day.

thresholds.description: Per-group temperature thresholds in °C, keyed by sensor group name. Empty by default and deliberately so: there is no sensible default, because what counts as hot depends on the machine and on what its owner is doing with it. A group name this build does not know is REFUSED rather than dropped.

shortcuts.description: Global shortcuts (P6.10), empty by default. NOTE ON THE FORMAT: this is an alternating array of action name and key combination — ["boost", {...}] — because Swift encodes a dictionary with an enum key that way. It round-trips correctly and is awkward to edit by hand; correcting it to an object is a tracked task. Published here as the format really is rather than as it should be, because a schema that describes an intention is worse than none.

modifiers.description: Bit set. At least one of Command, Option or Control is required; a combination without one is refused, because a bare letter would be swallowed in every application.

recording.description: Measurement recording (P7.02). Optional and additive: a file without this section is valid and means the defaults, which leave recording OFF — docs/operations/observability.md calls it "measurement recording, at the user's request". Files are written to Application Support/Boreas/Recordings and nothing is ever sent anywhere.

isEnabled.description: False by default. Recording writes files to the user's disk, so it waits to be asked.

format.description: jsonl is the default: it survives schema evolution and a file cut short by a power loss is readable up to its last complete line. csv fixes its columns when a file starts, so a sensor that appears later in the day is not in that file.

retentionDays.description: How long a file is kept. A preference — diskCeilingBytes overrides it. Today's file never expires, whatever this is set to.

diskCeilingBytes.description: The HARD limit on everything the recorder has written. When the total exceeds it the oldest files are deleted until it does not, even when they are newer than retentionDays — retention is a preference, this is a promise not to fill the disk. The file currently being written is never deleted.

maximumFileBytes.description: A file rotates to the next sequence number once it passes this size, so no single file grows unbounded within a day.

intervalSeconds.description: How often a sample is written. Independent of the monitor's sampling interval: two seconds is right for a live chart and wasteful for a file read a week later.
